title: Find The Original Array of Prefix Xor
statement: The array `pref` (length `n`) holds the running bitwise XOR of some hidden array `arr` of the same length: for every index `i`, `pref[i]` equals `arr[0] ^ arr[1] ^ ... ^ arr[i]`, where `^` is bitwise XOR. Rebuild and return `arr`. Exactly one such array exists.
notes:
## Intuition

Neighbouring prefix values differ by exactly one element: `pref[i] = pref[i - 1] ^ arr[i]`. XOR is its own inverse (`x ^ x = 0`), so XOR-ing both sides with `pref[i - 1]` gives `arr[i] = pref[i - 1] ^ pref[i]`. Every element can be read off from two adjacent prefix values, with no search at all. (A slow alternative recomputes the running XOR for each index and chooses the next value bit by bit.)

## Approach

1. Create `arr` with the same length as `pref`.
2. The first prefix contains only one element, so `arr[0] = pref[0]`.
3. For every later `i`, set `arr[i] = pref[i - 1] ^ pref[i]`, which cancels everything both prefixes share.
4. Return `arr`.

## Example 1, step by step

`pref = [5, 2, 0, 3, 1]`.

- `arr[0] = 5`.
- `arr[1] = 5 ^ 2 = 7` (`101 ^ 010 = 111`).
- `arr[2] = 2 ^ 0 = 2`.
- `arr[3] = 0 ^ 3 = 3`.
- `arr[4] = 3 ^ 1 = 2` (`11 ^ 01 = 10`).

The result is `[5, 7, 2, 3, 2]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one XOR per element.
- Space: O(1) besides the output array.

## Pitfalls

- If you overwrite `pref` in place, walk from right to left: going left to right, `pref[i - 1]` would already hold an element of `arr` instead of a prefix.
- Handle index 0 separately: it has no previous prefix.
- Do not subtract: XOR undoes XOR, ordinary subtraction does not.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pref` | the given running XOR values |
| `arr` | the rebuilt original array |
| `i` | the index being rebuilt |

narration.2: Make room for the original array, one slot per prefix value.
narration.3: The first prefix contains only arr[0], so it is that element.
narration.5: Rebuild every later element from two neighbouring prefixes.
narration.6: pref[i] = pref[i - 1] ^ arr[i], and XOR undoes itself, so arr[i] = pref[i - 1] ^ pref[i].
